answer_2.quote: Table  reports the performance of the models when trained on our dataset. The results are of the Reviewer Disagreement Classifier, which is the final step in our proposed approach. We report macro average P, R, and F1 scores as the rarity of the contradiction class is of particular interest for this task.

answer_3.quote: We compare our findings with those achieved by the zero-shot Large Language Model, ChatGPT. On the test set, ChatGPT scored an F1 of 64.67 which is 9 points lower than the baseline model, likely due to its lack of explicit training for this specific downstream task.

answer_4.quote: We had six doctoral students, each with four years of experience in scientific research publishing. To facilitate their training, two experts with more than ten years of experience in scientific publishing annotated 1,500 review pairs from a selection of random papers, following our guidelines.
answer_4.guideline: If I were shown two contemporaneous documents, one containing each of these passages, would I regard it as very unlikely that both passages could be true at the same time? If so, the two contradict each other.
